correctness.rationale: The n<=2 boundary is proved directly. For n=3, the finite domain is exhaustively enumerated twice: all 216 labeled profiles and all 36 school-relabeling representatives. Every unilateral strict-ranking deviation is checked, two independently coded Boston implementations agree, every orbit has size 6, and the verifier returns VERIFY_OK with 180+24+12=216. The six canonical bad profiles also hand-explain the third-to-second manipulation.

value.rationale: The common-priority unit-capacity model is a natural benchmark for immediate acceptance. The claim identifies the exact first manipulable market size, gives the complete incidence 1/6 and 24-versus-12 priority split, rules out simultaneous manipulators, and compresses every failure to six normalized structural types. This is a motivated boundary classification rather than an arbitrary finite recomputation.
